segments.text: Every banana you've ever eaten is a different plant. Well, that's not exactly true. Almost all of them are clones.
The banana in your kitchen is a Cavendish. It has no real seeds, so farmers grow new plants from cuttings of old ones. Same plant, copied millions of times.
Here's the wild part. Your grandparents ate a different banana, the Gros Michel. In the {1950s,|nineteen fifties,} a fungus wiped it out, because every plant had the same weak spot.
In fact, a banana plant isn't even a tree. It's a giant herb, and its trunk is just rolled up leaves.
That's not all. Bananas curve because they grow upward, bending toward the sun.
And bananas are a tiny bit radioactive, thanks to their potassium. Don't worry, you'd need millions at once for it to matter.
So next time you grab a banana, remember. You're eating a copy of a copy of a copy.
